speakers: Alan Don (guest host, Top Traders Unplugged, sitting in for Niels)
summary:
Systematic trend-following discussion (Ep.378, Dec 2025) after the Fed's third 2025 cut: prices are primal but not value, signal vs noise and unmeasurable uncertainty, thin holiday liquidity.
Covers bubbles (gold, cocoa, AI credit), where momentum works best (industry/factor > country/stock), and the total portfolio approach vs trend overlays.
Conclusion: use price signals but smooth them, treat uncertainty explicitly, and use trend as a diversifier when bonds hedge less.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: big impact on liquidity. It has an impact on you know uh what signals you receive and you have to start making some decisions on whether you should follow all signals
claims.claim: Holiday periods thin liquidity, which degrades signal quality, so a systematic trader must decide whether to follow every signal near year end.
claims.testable: partly - could test signal hit rate in low-volume weeks

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: Sochen CTA now down 2% on the year 2.06% and the sock gen trend uh close to flat down 0.16%
claims.claim: SocGen CTA index was down 2.06% and the SG Trend index down 0.16% year to date in mid-December 2025, with improvement in late-year trends.
claims.indicator: SG CTA index, SG Trend index

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: right around the Fed announcements is that you you get some uh high uncertainty. When you have high uncertainty, you could have large reversals in price.
claims.claim: Around FOMC announcements uncertainty is high and prices can reverse sharply, so short-term models may do better avoiding the Fed window.
claims.direction: avoid or flatten short-term positions around FOMC
claims.conditions: applies to short-horizon models; long-term rates still matter for cost of capital
claims.testable: yes - event-window backtest on FOMC dates

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we're going to be in a high uncertainty Fed environment for 2026, which is means there going to be more risk if you trade in the interest rate complex
claims.claim: Wide dispersion in FOMC dot projections (from hikes to six cuts) signals a high-uncertainty Fed in 2026 and so more risk in rates trading.
claims.conditions: when the dot spread is wide
claims.testable: partly - dispersion of dots is observable, link to risk untested here

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the projected inflation for the PCE for the core is going to be at 2.6 for 2026
claims.claim: Despite a third cut, Fed projections show core PCE at 2.6% and growth at 2.3% in 2026, i.e. still-high inflation with stronger growth than before.
claims.indicator: Fed SEP core PCE and GDP projections

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: they're forecasting higher growth but not translating into improved um unemployment
claims.claim: The Fed's projections of higher growth without lower unemployment imply it is buying the AI productivity story.

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: we've gone from QT to some form of QE again
claims.claim: The Fed ended balance-sheet runoff and began Treasury bill purchases to keep reserves sufficient after repo-market disruptions, a liquidity easing.
claims.indicator: Fed balance sheet, T-bill purchases, repo stress

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we can look at the strength of our signal divided by our our volatility. we could get a signal to noise ratio
claims.claim: A trend signal's quality can be measured as signal strength divided by volatility, a signal-to-noise ratio, which scales how much to trust it.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: it's not just the volatility which is measurable but it's also what is not measurable which is the uncertainty
claims.claim: Risk has a measurable part (volatility) and an unmeasurable part (uncertainty, e.g. Fed dissents or policy changes with tiny samples) that is hard to turn into a model input.
claims.conditions: small samples make uncertainty hard to quantify
claims.testable: no - uncertainty by definition not directly measured

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you said that, you know, job creation was overstated by 60,000 a month, then well, we've gone from a positive job market to something that uh uh is uh negative
claims.claim: Powell's remark that payroll growth may be overstated by about 60,000 a month implies the real job market is flat or negative, so labor data carries observational uncertainty.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: that becomes the the key balancing act is is that how much other information should you use in models beyond on price
claims.claim: When fundamental data is noisy, the central design choice for a systematic model is how much information beyond price to include.
claims.testable: partly - compare price-only vs price plus macro models

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: they say let's look at uh what real GDP is. Let's look with the expected inflation.
claims.claim: A rule of thumb values 10-year yields as expected inflation plus real GDP growth (about 2.6 + 2.3 = 4.9) plus any term premium, putting fair value near the high 4s versus the market near 4.1-4.2%.
claims.indicator: 10y yield vs expected inflation + real GDP
claims.direction: bonds look rich versus this anchor
claims.testable: yes - compute nominal GDP proxy versus yield

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the term premium was you was knocked down to something close to to to zero because the bonds were such a a good hedge
claims.claim: Term premium fell near zero while bonds were a reliable hedge; with high debt that hedge role is less assured, which argues for a higher premium.
claims.direction: term premium up, bond prices down
claims.conditions: when debt is high and bonds stop hedging equities
claims.testable: yes - term premium and stock-bond correlation are observable

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: Because a safe asset should be a diversifying asset. If bonds are not a diversifying asset, then what is and what should you do with your portfolio?
claims.claim: A safe asset is defined by diversification; if bonds no longer diversify equities, investors must find other diversifiers such as trend following.
claims.testable: yes - rolling correlation and drawdown tests

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the only way that you could solve those deficit problems outside of a default is that you can inflate your way out of that.
claims.claim: Large US deficits can only be resolved outside default by inflation, likely via financial repression that holds rates below inflation.
claims.testable: partly - real-rate history after high-debt episodes

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if relative safety in the US has gone down then the demand for other potentially safe assets should go up
claims.claim: If Treasuries are seen as less safe in relative terms, demand shifts to other safe assets like gold, whose supply is constrained, driving large price moves.
claims.conditions: gold supply cannot be created by fiat
claims.testable: partly - hard to measure relative safety

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: I would argue that uh there should be a greater term premium in the US market
claims.claim: Mark argues the US Treasury term premium should be higher given deficits and reduced relative safety.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you always have the price is telling you where there's a some balance between supply and demand
claims.claim: 'Prices are primal': whatever other data says, the price reveals the current supply-demand balance, so price is the anchor for systematic models.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: that prices are primal, but that's not the same as value
claims.claim: A price shows balance between supply and demand but not true value, so bubble-like prices (gold, silver above $60, individual stocks) can be informative without being fair.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: I might also use some other indicators to try to tell me is is that whether something could be overbought or oversold
claims.claim: A trend follower can add overbought/oversold or value-anchor indicators to guard against prices detached from value.
claims.testable: yes - add stretch filter to trend backtest

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you wanted to use some kind of smoothing mechanism that could be a moving average at the very simplest form
claims.claim: Smoothing prices (e.g. moving average) extracts a cleaner signal from noisy price processes.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: then prices follow narratives as opposed to lead narratives
claims.claim: A recent FX study using LLM-extracted news narratives found narratives develop first and prices follow with a carryover, so trends can reflect narrative trends as well as fundamentals.
claims.testable: yes - replicate with news text data

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's more likelihood that a small change in uh in in trading in volume will have a big a bigger impact on price. So your signals are going to get noisier as liquidity declines.
claims.claim: Year-end volume decline makes small order changes move prices more, so signals get noisier as liquidity falls.
claims.testable: yes - compare signal accuracy in thin periods

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: liquidity and and the quality of signals you know intraday is is U-shaped
claims.claim: Intraday liquidity and signal quality are U-shaped, highest at the open and close and lowest midday, which affects execution timing.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: normally you might ignore prices that occur on a Friday after Thanksgiving
claims.claim: Prices from thin days such as the Friday after Thanksgiving may be ignored or downweighted in models, although month-end volume complicates this.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: Do you try to smooth do you drop out signals?
claims.claim: After the 11-hour CME outage, a modeler must decide whether to trust post-outage prices, smooth, or drop signals; there is no rule and each choice is a model judgement.
claims.conditions: Nov 2025 CME outage at month end

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you use that wealth that's been created as collateral, well then what happens is that you could actually increase more leverage
claims.claim: Rising asset prices create collateral that is levered up, making the economy more fragile in bubbles.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the central banks uh beyond their increases in marktomarket is that they've been just been strong buyers of gold
claims.claim: Central banks have been strong net buyers of gold, adding demand pressure beyond price gains; some retail demand outside the US also.

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: very often volatility goes down so so margin requirements ments are lower so people can lever up
claims.claim: Rising equity markets lower volatility and margin requirements, letting leveraged holders add risk, and lower companies' cost of capital: a reflexive loop that reverses in a downturn.
claims.direction: leverage up then forced selling on reversal
claims.conditions: US households hold about $40tn of equity

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we do know that leverage is higher especially for for hedge funds
claims.claim: Leverage is higher overall, especially at large multi-strategy pod hedge funds that can lever due to diversification.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: It's closely linked to optimistic analyst expectations.
claims.claim: Harvard Business School research finds bubbles and crashes are closely linked to optimistic analyst fundamentals expectations, which fuel FOMO and raise crash probability.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: when it's harder to value an asset, then it's more likely to have a bubble because we don't know what is the true value
claims.claim: Assets that are harder to value are more bubble-prone because true value is unknowable.
claims.testable: partly - requires a valuation uncertainty proxy

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: Is there a regime change going on with gold? Well, central banks are changing their behavior.
claims.claim: Gold may be in a regime change because central banks are buying, safe-asset supply from Treasuries is falling, and retail abroad is buying on government uncertainty.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: retail demand in the US through ETFs is not as strong as what it as it has been in the past
claims.claim: The gold rally is not driven by US retail ETF demand or visible speculation, so standard bubble signatures do not apply.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: large speculators were actually declining before a lot of the big move in the cocoa price
claims.claim: In cocoa, COT large speculators, volatility and volume all fell while prices rose, contradicting the idea that bubbles show more speculation, volatility and volume.
claims.indicator: COT large speculator positions, cocoa volatility and volume

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: there are things going on in the debt market that should give investors concern
claims.claim: Heavy debt issuance for AI data centers combined with rising asset values is a bubble warning, per Howard Marks's note.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: when you have very frothy markets or when you have market extremes you have something called the the bezel
claims.claim: Galbraith's 'bezzle': at market extremes fraud and embezzlement surface (e.g. First Brands financing), a sign of credit froth.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the credit markets are uh at a market extreme and we're starting to see cracks in the behavior
claims.claim: Spreads are very tight but issuers and investors are beginning to demand premia for uncertain AI data center debt, which should be equity financed.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: Markets are a complex system and so there's interactions across markets and assets
claims.claim: Even futures-only traders should watch credit because cracks change risk aversion and shift capital into Treasuries, which feeds into price models.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: momentum is everywhere. It works you know across all time periods.
claims.claim: Momentum works across markets, countries, industries, factors and stocks and across sub-periods, with occasional failures.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: for industries there's much stronger momentum effect than what you'd find in in individual stocks
claims.claim: Industry and factor momentum are stronger than country, beta or individual stock momentum, so tilting momentum bets there does better.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: a lot of times for momentum strategies you lag one month because you you get sort of reversals in the very short run
claims.claim: Stock momentum shows intermediate-term persistence but short-term reversal, so strategies skip the most recent month.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's momentum in news, there's momentum in fundamentals, there's momentum in in uh surprise effects in earnings
claims.claim: Momentum exists in news, fundamentals and earnings surprises, imperfectly correlated with price momentum, allowing diversified momentum sources.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: people take time to digest information
claims.claim: Momentum persists because people take time to digest and attend to information, so prices respond over an extended period.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if an asset is higher to uh harder to value yes that there will be more likely to be persistence or momentum
claims.claim: Assets that are harder to value are more likely to show momentum, since it takes time to learn true value.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: or there's less analyst attention there's more likely to be persistence
claims.claim: Assets with little analyst coverage (e.g. small caps) have more persistence in price behavior.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: But if I look at the industry there may be actually trends.
claims.claim: Aggregating stocks into industries reduces noise, so trends are cleaner at industry level than individual stocks.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: we know that there's persistence in uh or uh you know after earnings announcements
claims.claim: Post-earnings drift and punctuated quarterly information mean equity momentum needs earnings-aware handling unlike commodity trend following.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there are certain seasonality uh you know associated with uh with certain markets
claims.claim: Commodities have seasonality and lack earnings-style punctuation, so signals should differ from equities.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's observational uncertainty, there's there's prognostic uh or forecasting uncertainty
claims.claim: A stochastic optimization text lists ten uncertainty types (observational, prognostic, experimental, transitional, inferential, model, exogenous, control implementation, algorithmic, goal), each of which affects signals.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you looked at uh copper prices in New York versus Lond London copper prices there's a big divergence between the two prices
claims.claim: Tariff-driven divergence between COMEX and LME copper creates ambiguity about which price to use to generate trend signals.
claims.testable: yes - compare signals on the two prices

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: there's measurement problems with a lot of the fundamental data because people don't respond to the surveys
claims.claim: Falling survey response rates and partisan splits in consumer surveys add measurement uncertainty to macro data.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: if you look at expectations in fiveyear 5year forward prices it looks like they're fairly well anchored at around 2 and a.5%
claims.claim: Market-based 5y5y inflation looks anchored near 2.5% while consumer surveys show unanchored higher inflation, which matters for consumer behavior.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: you allow for more of adjustments in the assets you hold to reach some overall goal of you know the return or controlled volatility
claims.claim: Total portfolio approach (e.g. CalPERS) replaces fixed strategic weights with flexible adjustment toward overall return or volatility goals.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: the 6040 stock bond portfolio, it it may not provide the diversification you need
claims.claim: The 60/40 portfolio may not provide enough diversification, so investors seek alternatives.

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: if you added a I think it was a 30% overlay to the sock genen trend index you achieve um a 4% tracking error
claims.claim: A 30% overlay of the SG Trend index on a 70/30 stock-bond portfolio yields about 4% tracking error, matching the CalPERS TPA target, a simple way to make a static portfolio adaptive.

claims.speaker: Alan Don
claims.quote: Obviously trend following achieves a lot of what TPA is trying to do already.
claims.claim: Trend following already allocates dynamically across and within asset complexes, covering much of what TPA wants.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: those weights you know uh should respond to changes in uh in uh volatility and and correlation coariance
claims.claim: Portfolio weights should respond to changes in volatility and correlation rather than staying fixed.

claims.speaker: Mark
claims.quote: diversification is primal to portfolio construction
claims.claim: Diversification is the foundation of portfolio construction; start from a strategic allocation and adapt with market conditions.
